name: Nanopore from raw signal to coverage
description: Start from the raw POD5 signal files of a Nanopore run: call the bases with Dorado, filter, check the reads, map them to a genome and measure coverage.
details: Use this when you have the raw signal (POD5 files) straight from the sequencer and want to run the basecalling yourself. The pipeline merges your POD5 files into one and summarises it, calls the bases with the Dorado basecaller, turns the result into a FASTQ file, drops reads that are short or of low quality with chopper, reports the quality and length of what is left with NanoPlot, maps the reads to your reference genome with minimap2 (Nanopore preset), sorts and indexes the alignments, and measures how deeply each part of the genome is covered with mosdepth. Dorado is not a conda package: the app downloads it from Oxford Nanopore the first time, and that download exists for macOS on Apple silicon only. On Windows and on Linux, or if you already have FASTQ files from MinKNOW, use the template "Nanopore reads from FASTQ to coverage", which starts after the basecalling and works on every platform. The basecalling model (fast, hac or sup) is downloaded on the first run and needs the internet; basecalling is much faster on a graphics card or on Apple silicon than on a plain processor. The default model is hac, which is a good balance. Dorado drops reads below Q10 and chopper then drops reads shorter than 500 bases; change both in their steps for very short or noisy samples. Filtlong, another read filter, is in the tool catalog if you prefer it to chopper.

inputs.label: Raw signal files
inputs.hint: One or more POD5 files from the sequencer. If you have FAST5 files, convert them with the "pod5 convert from FAST5" tool first.

inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.hint: The genome the reads should map to, as a FASTA file.

outputs.label: Filtered reads
outputs.hint: FASTQ with the reads that passed the quality and length filter.

outputs.label: Read quality report
outputs.hint: Open NanoPlot-report.html in a browser: read lengths and qualities.

outputs.label: Read statistics
outputs.hint: The same numbers as text: number of reads, N50, mean quality.

outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.hint: Sorted BAM of the mapped reads.

outputs.label: Signal file summary
outputs.hint: How many reads and how much signal the POD5 files hold.
